source_file: 我有友情要出租(5-8 岁).pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 我有友情要出租
作者:方素珍 绘者:郝洛玟
中国和平出版社

[P3] 我有友情要出租

[P4] 有一只大猩猩，他常常想：
“我好寂寞，我都没有朋友。”

[P5] 有一天，他在大树上贴了一片叶子，
上面写着：
我有友情要
出租
一小时五块钱
他坐在大树下，等着、等着，
等到眼睛都快闭上了。

[P6] 这时候，咪咪骑着自行车过来了，
她看到了叶子，立刻跳下车，问大猩猩：
“什么叫友情出租？”
大猩猩睁大了眼睛说：
“就是你给我五块钱，
我陪你玩一个小时。”
“一个小时是多久呢？”
大猩猩拿出一个沙漏说：
“上面的沙子全部漏到下面的时候，
刚好是一个小时。”
咪咪想了一下，说：
“可不可以便宜一点？
我只有一块钱。”
大猩猩高兴得一直点头：
“好哇！好哇！”
大猩猩立刻把咪咪的一块钱
收进背包里。
沙漏里的沙子，开始计时了！

[P7] 咪咪对大猩猩说：
“我们先玩踩脚游戏，来，猜拳！”
但是，大猩猩不会剪刀、石头、布。
咪咪看着沙漏，着急地说：
“时间都给你耗掉了，快一点啦！
我喊一二三，你把手伸出来就对了。”

“一、二、三。”大猩猩把右手伸出来，
他的手指头撑得开开的，
咪咪也伸出手，她出的是两根手指头，
咪咪说：“我出的是剪刀，你出的是布，
所以我赢了，你要让我踩一下！”

[P8] 大猩猩还搞不清楚状况，就被咪咪
“叭哒”踩下去了。他叫了一声：“哎呀！
“很痛吗？”咪咪问。
大猩猩揉一揉脚趾头说：
“不痛，不痛，我已经会了，很好玩！
接下来，大猩猩每一次出的都是“布”，
咪咪每一次出的都是“剪刀”，
大猩猩只好被踩了一下又一下，
但是，好不容易有人和他玩，
他巴不得沙子不要漏得那么快呢！

[P9] 第二天，咪咪又来租大猩猩的友情了。
大猩猩把一块钱放进背包里，
沙漏也开始计时了。
他们先猜拳，“一、二、三。”
咪咪以为大猩猩只会出“布”，所以，
她立刻就出“剪刀”，
没想到，大猩猩出的居然是“石头”！
咪咪输啦！换她要被踩一脚了。
大猩猩举起脚来，却看到咪咪闭着眼睛、
歪着嘴巴的表情，
他只好重重地举起来，
轻轻地踩下去。

[P10] 奇怪，怎么都不痛？咪咪愣了一下，
大猩猩又继续猜拳了。
因为他握紧拳头赢了一次，所以，
他就一直出“石头”，
咪咪也知道了，她只要出“布”，
就会赢大猩猩，
被踩的倒霉鬼一定是大猩猩。
大猩猩根本不在乎，他又叫又笑的，
玩得好开心，沙漏里的沙子都漏完了，
他还不知道呢！

[P11] 后来，咪咪每天都到大树下来租友情，
她总是先把一块钱交给大猩猩，
等大猩猩把钱放进背包里，
沙漏开始计时了，她就和大猩猩玩。

[P12] 有一天，她教
大猩猩玩一二三
木头人。
有一天，
她教大猩猩讲故事……
有一天，
她在树下写功课。
大猩猩就乖乖地
趴在旁边看，
即使不说一句话，
大猩猩都
觉得好幸福呢！

[P13] 这一天下午，大猩猩没有带小背包，
只是带了几片饼干，就走到大树下等咪咪，
等了好久好久，咪咪一直没有来。

[P14] 终于，一部大车子开过来了，
咪咪从车子里探出头，大声地对他说：
“喂！我没有钱了，而且
我们要搬家了！再见！”
大猩猩立刻追着车子，大声地喊：
“喂，我还没有学会出剪刀耶！”
但是咪咪留下了布娃娃，远远地离开了！

[P15] 大猩猩失望地
回到大树下：
“唉！我今天
没有带小背包，

也没有带沙漏，
就是不要收咪咪的钱，
而且还要请她吃饼干呢，
可是，
她怎么走了！？
大猩猩一面啃着饼干，
一面想念咪咪。

[P16] 后来，大猩猩又在大树上
贴了一片叶子，
上面写着：
我有友情免费出租
一直到今天，
那一片叶子都
褪色了……
我有友情
免费出租

[P18] 大猩猩还在等待下一个好朋友。
full_text_en:
[P1] I Have Friendship to Rent
Author: Fang Suzzhen Illustrator: Hao Luowen
China Peace Publishing House

[P3] I have friendship to rent

[P4] There was a big gorilla who often thought:
"I'm so lonely, I don't have any friends."

[P5] One day, he stuck a leaf on a big tree,
which read:
I have friendship to rent
One hour for five coins
He sat under the tree, waiting and waiting,
until his eyes were almost closed.

[P6] At this moment, Mimi rode her bicycle over.
She saw the leaf, jumped off immediately, and asked the big gorilla:
"What does 'renting friendship' mean?"
The big gorilla opened his eyes wide and said:
"It means you give me five dollars,
and I'll play with you for one hour."
"How long is one hour?"
The big gorilla took out an hourglass and said:
"When all the sand on top flows to the bottom,
it's exactly one hour."
Mimi thought for a moment and said:
"Can it be cheaper?
I only have one dollar."
The big gorilla nodded happily:
"Great! Great!"
The big gorilla immediately put Mimi's one dollar
into his backpack.
The sand in the hourglass began to flow!

[P7] Mimi said to the gorilla:
"Let's play a foot-stomping game first, come on, rock-paper-scissors!"
But the gorilla didn't know how to play rock-paper-scissors.
Mimi looked at the hourglass and said anxiously:
"You've used up all the time, hurry up!
I'll count one, two, three, and then you put out your hand."

"One, two, three." The gorilla put out his right hand,
with his fingers spread wide open.
Mimi also put out her hand, showing two fingers.
Mimi said: "I showed scissors, you showed cloth,
so I won, you have to let me step on you!"

[P8] The gorilla still didn't understand the situation, and was already 'plop' stepped on by Mimi. He cried out, "Ouch!"
"Does it hurt?" Mimi asked.
The gorilla rubbed his toes and said:
"No pain, no pain, I've already learned it, it's so much fun!"
Next, every time the gorilla played 'rock',
Mimi always played 'scissors',
so the gorilla had to be stepped on again and again,
but since it was so hard to find someone to play with,
he wished the sand wouldn't leak so quickly!

[P9] The next day, Mimi came again to rent the big gorilla's friendship.
The gorilla put a one-dollar coin into his backpack,
and the hourglass started counting down.
They played rock-paper-scissors first, "One, two, three."
Mimi thought the gorilla would only play "paper," so
she immediately played "scissors."
But unexpectedly, the gorilla played "rock"!
Mimi lost! Now it was her turn to be stepped on.
The gorilla lifted his foot, but saw Mimi with her eyes closed and
her mouth twisted,
so he had to lift it high again,
and gently step down.

[P10] Strange, why doesn't it hurt? Mimi was startled for a moment.
Then the big gorilla continued playing rock-paper-scissors.
Because he had won once by making a fist, so,
he kept playing "rock".
Mimi figured it out—she just had to play "paper" to win against the gorilla.
The unlucky one who gets stepped on would definitely be the gorilla.
The gorilla didn't care at all. He was shouting and laughing,
having such a good time that he didn't even notice the sand in the hourglass had run out!

[P11] Later, Mimi came to the big tree every day to rent friendship.
She always gave the gorilla one coin first,
then waited for the gorilla to put the money in his backpack.
Once the hourglass started counting, she would play with the gorilla.

[P12] One day, she taught
the gorilla to play 'One, Two, Three, Freeze'.
One day,
she taught the gorilla to tell stories...
One day,
she did her homework under the tree.
The gorilla would obediently
lie beside her and watch,
even if he didn't say a word,
the gorilla felt
so happy!

[P13] One afternoon, the gorilla didn't bring his little backpack,
only a few cookies, and walked to the big tree to wait for Mimi.
He waited for a long, long time, but Mimi never came.

[P14] Finally, a big truck came by.
Mimi poked her head out of the truck and shouted loudly:
"Hey! I don't have any money left, and
we're moving away! Goodbye!"
The gorilla immediately chased after the truck, shouting loudly:
"Hey, I still haven't learned to play 'scissors' yet!"
But Mimi left behind her cloth doll and drove away into the distance!

[P15] The big gorilla returned to the tree disappointedly:
"Sigh! I didn't bring my little backpack today,

nor did I bring the hourglass.
I didn't even want to take Mimi's money,
and I was even going to treat her to some cookies.
But then... why did she leave!?"
The gorilla chewed on a cookie,
while missing Mimi.

[P16] Later, the big gorilla put a leaf on the big tree,
with the words written on it:
I have friendship for rent, free of charge.
Until today,
that leaf has faded...
I have friendship
for rent, free of charge.

[P18] The big gorilla is still waiting for his next good friend.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本封面，标题为《我有友情要出租》，作者方素珍，绘者郝洛玟。画面中一只大猩猩表情忧郁地吃着饼干，背景中一个小女孩在树上玩耍、披着红布、抱着娃娃，暗示故事主题与友情和孤独有关。
[P2] 画面描绘了一群人在绿树成荫的户外营地活动，有人在桌前讨论地图和笔记，有人整理装备，远处一人骑自行车沿小路驶来，整体氛围轻松自然，暗示团队协作或探险准备。
[P3] 画面展示了一片热带丛林，前景是茂密的绿色植物，中景有一条小路，左侧一个小女孩骑着自行车，右侧远处一只大猩猩坐在地上，背景是树林和岩石。画面中央有红色大字“我有友情要出租”，点明故事主题。
[P4] 本页介绍了一只孤独的大猩猩，他常常感到寂寞，没有朋友，画面通过多个姿态展现了他的忧郁情绪。
[P5] 大猩猩在树上贴出‘我有友情要出租’的告示，一小时五块钱，然后坐在树下等待，却无人回应，感到非常孤单。
[P6] 小女孩咪咪骑车路过，看到大猩猩的友情出租告示，用一块钱租下他的陪伴，大猩猩高兴地接受，沙漏开始计时。
[P7] 咪咪和大猩猩玩猜拳游戏，大猩猩不会玩，咪咪着急地催促并宣布自己赢了，要求大猩猩让她踩一下。
[P8] 咪咪和大猩猩玩猜拳游戏，大猩猩总是出‘布’，咪咪出‘剪刀’，导致大猩猩被踩，但他为了能和人玩耍，假装不痛并希望时间慢点过去。
[P9] 第二天，咪咪再次租借大猩猩的友情，两人玩猜拳游戏。咪咪以为大猩猩只会出“布”，便出“剪刀”，结果大猩猩出“石头”赢了，按约定咪咪要被踩一脚。大猩猩看到咪咪害怕的表情，便轻轻踩下去，表现出温柔和体贴。
[P10] 咪咪发现大猩猩被踩时并不痛，于是继续猜拳。大猩猩因赢过一次便一直出“石头”，咪咪则出“布”赢他。大猩猩毫不在意，玩得非常开心，直到沙漏的沙子流尽，他仍浑然不觉。
[P11] 咪咪每天都会来大树下租借大猩猩的友情，她先付钱，大猩猩把钱放进背包，沙漏开始计时后，两人就开始一起玩耍。画面中，大猩猩背着咪咪开心地走着，旁边放着沙漏和背包。
[P12] 咪咪和大猩猩在树下一起玩耍，她教大猩猩玩‘一二三木头人’和讲故事，也写功课时大猩猩在一旁安静陪伴，感到非常幸福。
[P13] 大猩猩没有带背包，只带了几片饼干到大树下等咪咪，但等了很久咪咪都没有出现。
[P14] 咪咪一家要搬家了，她从车上对大猩猩说再见，大猩猩追着车喊还没学会出剪刀，咪咪留下布娃娃后离开。
[P15] 大猩猩回到大树下，发现咪咪没有出现，他一边吃着饼干，一边想念咪咪，感到非常失落。
[P16] 大猩猩在大树上贴了一片写有“我有友情免费出租”的叶子，至今叶子已褪色，他独自坐在树下，怀抱着咪咪留下的布娃娃，显得十分孤单和思念。
[P17] 画面中，大猩猩抱着布娃娃独自走在森林小径上，显得孤单；左侧一群动物（长颈鹿、斑马、犀牛、狮子、鳄鱼、兔子、鸭子）正好奇地望向他，似乎在关注他的状态。
[P18] 在橙色的黄昏下，大猩猩独自坐在大树旁，怀抱着布娃娃，仍在等待下一个好朋友。
